ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A car traveling at a constant speed of $20\mathrm{m/s}$ reduces its speed by half after braking for 4 seconds. 1. The magnitude of the acceleration after the car brakes. 2. The speed and displacement of the car after braking for 10 seconds.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Use constant-acceleration kinematics. Initial speed u = 20 m/s. After 4 s of braking, the speed is reduced by half, so v = 10 m/s. The acceleration is a = (v - u) / t = (10 - 20) / 4 = -2.5 m/s^2, so its magnitude is 2.5 m/s^2. For 10 s of braking, the stopping time under this constant deceleration is t_stop = 20 / 2.5 = 8 s. Since 10 s is longer than 8 s, the car stops after 8 s and then remains at rest. Thus the speed after 10 s is 0. The displacement is only the distance traveled before stopping: s = ut + (1/2)at^2 = 20(8) + (1/2)(-2.5)(8^2) = 160 - 80 = 80 m.

From the text, plot velocity starting at 20 m/s at t=0 and decreasing linearly to 10 m/s at t=4 s because the braking is treated as uniform. The slope of this line is (10-20)/4=-2.5 m/s^2, so the acceleration magnitude is 2.5 m/s^2. Extend the same straight-line deceleration to where it reaches v=0: the line drops 20 m/s at 2.5 m/s^2, so it reaches zero at t=8 s. For the requested 10 s, the velocity-time graph is then zero from 8 s to 10 s. The speed at 10 s is therefore 0, and the displacement is the area under the velocity-time graph: a triangle with base 8 s and height 20 m/s, area (1/2)(8)(20)=80 m.
method.CoT_raw: Use the velocity-time graph interpretation. At the instant braking begins, take t=0 and v=20 m/s. After 4 s of braking, the speed has been reduced by half, so v=10 m/s at t=4 s. Treating the braking as uniform, the velocity-time graph is a straight line from (0, 20) to (4, 10). Its slope is the acceleration: a = (10 - 20) / 4 = -2.5 m/s^2, so the magnitude of the acceleration is 2.5 m/s^2. Extending the same straight-line deceleration, the time to go from 20 m/s to 0 m/s is 20 / 2.5 = 8 s. Therefore, by 10 s after braking starts, the car has already stopped and its speed is 0. The displacement is the area under the velocity-time graph from 0 to 10 s. From 0 to 8 s it is a triangle with base 8 s and height 20 m/s, and from 8 to 10 s the velocity is zero. Thus displacement = (1/2) × 8 × 20 = 80 m.
